people with mental illness and psychosocial disabilities in South Africa want to be involved in policy and service developments, but that their involvement has been limited.
people living with mental health difficulties in South Africa have identified a number of priorities for policy and service reform that will support their recovery.
service users have the right to be involved in policy and service developments and that their involvement has value to their recovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an enabling environment that will facilitate service users' recovery.
developing a framework for service user involvement in public policy research and development.
the need for a shift in the way mental health services are conceptualised and delivered.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the service users' involvement is essential to promote their recovery and that the involvement of service users in policy and service reforms should be a priority.
the findings of this study have implications for policy and services that are required to promote the rights and needs of service users.

the findings of this study have implications for policy and practice in the field of rehabilitation, in particular for the development of rehabilitation programmes that promote empowerment of people with disabilities and the development of rehabilitation policies that are based on the principles of empowerment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified that the South African government needs to address mental health care service provision in South Africa, and to do so in a way that is inclusive, empowering and rights-based.
service user involvement in research and service development is an essential element of the recovery process, and is a necessary condition for effective policy implementation.
the mental health care policy and services in South Africa should be based on the principles of human rights and social justice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
service users are experts in the lived experience of their condition, and that they should be involved in policy and service planning, implementation and evaluation.
people living with psychosoical difficulties have a right and a role to play in policy and service developments.
service users are the best source of information about their needs, and their involvement in policy development is essential.
